Designed and implemented. The metric is the one the residual-norm notebook already established: per-equation sum of squared residuals over the domain, as a share of the total, no volume weighting (the solver's norm is a plain sum over state-vector entries) and shares rather than magnitudes (raw residual scales with the adaptive timestep). Seven numbers per output step in place of seven full fields.

The extractor now writes them into series.tsv as share_<equation> plus resid_ss_total, so they survive R8 deletion, and the study report has a page showing which equation holds the solver up over the run.

Sampling limit found and annotated on every panel: the resid_ fields refresh once per INTERNAL solver step, not per output. On the fast configurations resid_ss_total takes only 2 distinct values across 91 outputs, against ~70 on the slow ones — so the diagnostic's real resolution collapses exactly when the timestep grows. Anyone reading the history needs the distinct-state count beside it, which the page prints.

Fixed 2026-07-31 in apply_recipe.py, which now translates retired options as it applies a recipe and says loudly what it did and why. Covers solver:pid_controller -> timestep_control = pid_nonlinear_its, and solver:use_precon -> cvode_precon_method = user or none by value.

The translation table is deliberately faithfulness-first: an entry must reproduce exactly what the retired option did. A known-retired option carrying an unrecognised value exits with an error rather than guessing, because a wrong translation silently changes what a recipe means and is worse than the abort it prevents. cvode_precon_method is the reason for that rule - its default (none) and its auto value both differ from what use_precon = true meant.

Each rewritten line carries a comment naming the option it replaced, and the tool prints a reminder that the case now differs from its named recipe. Verified on both stale recipes and on SNES-MUMPS-2, which passes through silently. The read-only recipe files were not touched.

Settled 2026-07-31. The test is test2scratch at nout = 200, SNES-MUMPS-1, MC build, slot 1.

The user chose 20 ms of simulated time rather than a wall-clock target, which is the better axis anyway: the work is fixed and the wall time is the measurement. The input steps at 95788 * 0.1, i.e. 0.1 ms per output, so today's nout = 450 is 45 ms and nout = 200 is 20 ms. No calibration run is needed, which also sidesteps having to calibrate on a VanAlbada build for an MC ladder.

Expect appreciably more than 20/45 of the full 56 m 36 s, because the from-scratch transient is front-loaded rather than uniform. From scratch also means no seed state, so the restart-drift confound that rules out the steady and stiff tests does not apply here.

Answered 2026-09-21, from the PETSc 3.23.3 source at /home/mike/work/petsc-3.23.3.

The option is not misspelled and not deprecated. It is inapplicable to this code path, so PETSc never reads it.

-snes_fd_color_use_mat is read in exactly one place, src/snes/interface/snesj2.c line 79, inside SNESComputeJacobianDefaultColor. It sits in the `if (!color)` branch, which runs only when PETSc has to build the colouring itself from the DM or the matrix.

BOUT++ builds the colouring itself. With use_coloring = true, FDJinitialise calls updateColoring and passes the result as the context to SNESSetJacobian (snes.cxx lines 132 to 147), so `color` is non-null and the branch is skipped before the option is ever consulted. Setting it true or false cannot change anything while use_coloring is true.

Two supporting details. It is read with PetscOptionsGetBool rather than registered with PetscOptionsBool, so it never appears in -help and is always reported as left over. And it is the only knob in search-space.toml with no registration anywhere on the SNES path, which is how the inventory found it: the other 84 all resolve.

Action it implies, not yet done: the option is dead weight in SNES-1, SNES-MUMPS-1, SNES-MUMPS-2 and SNES-MUMPS-3, and it is what makes options_left non-empty on every run. Removing it from those recipes would leave a clean report, which is worth doing now that a run is refused when a varied knob shows up there.
